ratings_why.fun: One visible number and a front-row flood map are easy to grasp, but most growth is plain '+X/+X when the Level changes' and Hendrika is a hard read.
ratings_why.distinct: A public water dial that hurts both front rows before anyone attacks, with Afloat and Dike slots, plays unlike any of today's tribes.

verdict_why: The only fix is a one-word rules clarification on the Flood; another round would change the cards, not improve them.

points.text: The Flood takes 'a tenth of its Health' per Level; say current Health, since Tail-Slapper's repeat Floods and the golden Pup's double Flood land on already-hurt units.

Hendrika's three sentences are the hardest read in the tribe; 'Twice a turn: when you Raise or Drain, you may keep going to 5 or 0' could stand alone, with the for-this-fight rule moved into the Raise/Drain keyword.
Kobus Bles also doubles Hendrika, since she triggers on Raise or Drain; the second trigger does nothing, so saying 'not Hendrika' would save players a puzzle.
The tenths are a calculation; the board should show each front unit's Flood loss before the fight so a player reads the danger at a glance.
Polder Millwright's Raise 1 and Drain 1 reads as 'does nothing' to a new player; a short '(two changes)' on the card would show why it is the swing build's engine.

standouts.why: Kobus minutes everything twice: the clerk's joke is the card, and it reads like a familiar trigger doubler.
Winter Raft pays double when the canals freeze at Level 0; a clear rule that carries the skating-polder picture.
The Spaarndam Pup plugging the dike so your own Floods spare you is the fantasy and the capstone in one line.

weakest.why: Kees Kowk's contested ditches don't show; it is a generic Attack gain off the Flood.
Hendrika is powerful but takes three readings to understand, the opposite of a glance.
Net-zero Level change hides its payoff unless you already know the change-payoff cards.

flags.note: Hendrika with Kobus and Master of the Nine Mills or Old Bram gives very large permanent stats each turn; bounded but worth a Tier 6 sim.
Repeat Floods depend on whether the tenth is of current or full Health; the rule doesn't say.
